sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has announced the Your First Home scheme to assist first-time buyers in England. The initiative offers a 20 per cent equity loan for new-build properties to buyers providing a 2.5 per cent deposit. Income, deposit, and property price caps will apply. Additionally, the government announced plans to make it easier for local councils to take over long-term empty homes and convert them into housing.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Supporters argue the policy helps young buyers lacking family financial support, while giving housebuilders confidence to build. However, Conservative critics warn that the scheme risks driving up property prices and increasing buyer debt burdens. Reports differ on announcement details: one outlet notes John Healey will formally announce the programme in the budget, while another attributes housing policy unveils to Angela Rayner.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Further details on how the equity loan scheme operates are expected in the upcoming Budget, with registration targeted to open by the end of 2026.
